seo.description: Altrazen audits, stabilises and maintains applications built with AI coding tools. Free 30 minute review. Find out what is wrong before it costs you a customer.

hero.headline: Your AI built it. We keep it running.
hero.subheadline: Altrazen audits, stabilises, and maintains applications built with AI coding tools, so you can keep shipping without wondering what's about to break.

problem.heading: You shipped fast. That was the right call.
paragraphs: You had an idea and a tool that could build it, and you used it. Six months of engineering time turned into a weekend. The product exists, people can use it, and some of them are paying. Nobody sensible would tell you that was the wrong decision.
But AI coding tools write code that works. They do not write code that lasts. There is a difference, and it only shows up later.

Your AI did not set up backups. It did not tell you your API keys are sitting in your git history. It did not add a way to know when the site goes down, so the first person who finds out is a customer, and they find out by leaving.

commonIssues.heading: Six things that are almost always wrong
commonIssues.description: Not a scare list. This is what we actually find, over and over, in codebases built with Lovable, Cursor, Bolt, v0 and Replit.

items.label: Secrets in the code
items.description: API keys, database URLs and tokens committed to the repository. Deleting them later does not help, because the git history keeps them.

items.label: No backups
items.description: No automated backup, or one that has never been restored. An untested backup is a belief, not a backup.

items.label: Auth in the wrong place
items.description: Permission checks written in the browser rather than on the server. Anyone who opens developer tools can walk straight past them.

items.label: Silent failures
items.description: Errors caught and swallowed with no logging and no alert. The application looks fine while quietly losing writes.

items.label: No way to roll back
items.description: Deploys go straight to production with no staging and no one-step revert. A bad release becomes an emergency instead of an inconvenience.

items.label: Stale dependencies
items.description: Packages months or years behind, several with published vulnerabilities, and now far enough behind that upgrading is its own project.

servicesOverview.heading: Three steps, in order
servicesOverview.description: The audit tells you what is wrong. Stabilisation fixes it. Maintenance keeps it that way.

howItWorks.heading: From first call to a system someone is watching

steps.title: Audit
steps.outcome: A written report telling you exactly what is broken and what it would cost you.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.outcome: The critical findings closed, backups working, monitoring live, rollback in place.

steps.title: Maintain
steps.outcome: Patched, monitored and answered for, so it stays fixed.

pricing.heading: What this costs
paragraphs: An audit starts at $250. Stabilisation starts at $600 and is quoted exactly once we have read the code. Maintenance runs from $150 a month.
For most people this lands somewhere between a fraction of a part-time engineer and the cost of one bad outage. The difference is that you only pay for the second one after it has already happened.
We will give you an exact number after a 30-minute call. Not a range, and not an hourly rate that grows quietly.

whoYouWorkWith.heading: You talk to the person doing the work
paragraphs: Altrazen is deliberately small. There is no account manager, no handoff to a delivery team, and nobody translating your problem into a ticket for someone who has never spoken to you.

The engineer who reads your codebase is the engineer who writes your report, joins your walkthrough call, and answers your message four months later. That is not a limitation we are hiding. It is the reason the work is any good.

finalCta.heading: Not sure if you need this?
finalCta.description: Send us your repo link and we'll tell you the three things we'd fix first. No charge, no pitch.
